Rashi on Ketubot 18b:2:1.english: No different with regard to him and no different with regard to his son - And even if he [the son] is a minor.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:2:2.hebrew: אינו מעיז - ולהכי קרי ליה טענת עצמו, משום דטענת קטן בעלמא לית בה מששא:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:2:2.english: He is not insolent - And that is why [Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov] calls it "his own claim," because a claim of a minor in general has no substance.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:2:3.english: But before his son he is insolent - And even if [the son] is an adult.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:3:1.english: The witnesses who said, etc. - Who were testifying regarding their signatures to ratify the document.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:3:2.english: We were disqualified witnesses - Relatives or dice-players.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:3:3.hebrew: הרי אלו נאמנים - כיון דאין כתב ידם ניכר אלא על פיהם, הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר. כי היכי דמהימנת להו אהא, הימנינהו אהא:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:3:3.english: They are deemed credible - Since their handwriting is not recognized except by their own word, "the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted": just as you believe them regarding this [that it is their handwriting], believe them regarding this [that they were disqualified].

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:3:4.hebrew: יוצא ממקום אחר - חתומים בשטר אחר שהוחזק בב"ד וכתוב בו הנפק, ובא אותו שטר לפנינו עם זה, וכתב חותמן דומין של זה לשל זה — אין כאן הפה שאסר, ואין נאמנים לומר פסולים היינו:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:3:4.english: Emerges from another place - [They are] signed on another document that was authenticated in court and has a certification [of authenticity] written on it, and that document comes before us together with this [one], and the handwriting of their signatures on this [document] and on that [document] are alike — [thus] there is no [application of] "the mouth that prohibited [is the mouth that permitted]" here, and they are not deemed credible to say, "We were disqualified."

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:4:1.english: They only taught - That if their handwriting emerges from elsewhere, they are not believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:4:2.hebrew: אלא שאמרו אנוסים היינו מחמת ממון - דלאו כל כמינייהו לשוויי נפשייהו רשעים בעדות פיהם ולפסול את השטר, דאדם קרוב אצל עצמו ואינו נאמן על עצמו לא לזכות ולא לחובה בדיני נפשות ובפסולי עדות להעשות רשע ופסול על פיו, ואלו פוסלים עצמן באומרם חתמנו שקר בשביל אונס ממון. ורישא, טעמא משום הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:4:2.english: Only where they said, "We were compelled due to money" - For it is not within their power to render themselves wicked through the testimony of their own mouths and invalidate the document, since a person is considered a relative to himself and is not believed regarding himself — neither to his benefit nor to his detriment — in capital cases or regarding disqualifications from testimony, to become wicked and disqualified by his own word; and these [witnesses] disqualify themselves by saying, "We signed falsely because of financial compulsion." And [in] the first clause [of the Mishnah], the reason is [the principle of] "the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted."

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:4:3.hebrew: מחמת נפשות - שאמר בעל השטר הזה להרגנו, ואדם חזק הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:4:3.english: Due to [a threat to] lives - [That is,] the holder of this document threatened to kill us, and he is a powerful man.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:5:1.hebrew: כיון שהגיד שוב אינו חוזר ומגיד - דגבי עדות חדא הגדה כתיבא: "אם לא יגיד וגו'" (ויקרא ה). והכא נמי, כיון דחתימי בשטרא, היינו הגדה דידהו, והיכי מהימני תו למיעקר, הואיל וכתב ידן יוצא ממקום אחר? בשלמא רישא, כשאין כתב ידן יוצא ממקום אחר ועלייהו סמכינן, כולה חדא הגדה היא, דהא באותו דבור [בכדי] שאילת שלום קאמרי "אבל אנוסים היינו". אבל הכא, לאו אפומייהו סמכינן:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:5:1.english: Once he has stated [his testimony], he cannot again state [testimony] - For regarding testimony, [only] one statement is written: "If he does not state [it], etc." (Leviticus 5). And here too, since they are signed on the document, that is their statement, so how can they be believed again to uproot [it], since their handwriting emerges from another source? Granted, [in] the first clause, where their handwriting does not emerge from another source and we rely on them, it is all one statement, for in that same utterance, within [the time of] a greeting, they say, "but we were coerced." Here, however, we do not rely on their word.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:5:2.hebrew: הני מילי על פה - כגון המעיד בב"ד ולאחר כדי דבור בא לשנות בו:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:5:2.english: This applies to oral [testimony] - For example, one who testifies in court and after kedei dibbur [the time of an utterance] comes to change it.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:5:3.english: But in a document, no - For "telling" [oral declaration] is written [in Scripture].

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:6:1.english: They taught [this] only - That we say, "the mouth that forbade," etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:6:2.hebrew: אלא דאמרי מחמת נפשות - נאנסנו, דלא משוו נפשייהו רשעים. וכיון דעלייהו סמכינן, הא בתוך כדי דבור עקרוה לסהדותייהו, והפה שאסר התיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:6:2.english: Rather, where they say, "Because of [a threat to] lives" - [i.e.,] "we were compelled," for they do not render themselves wicked. And since we rely upon them [to authenticate the signatures], behold, within the span of an utterance they have uprooted their testimony, and the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:6:3.hebrew: אין אדם משים עצמו רשע - אינו נאמן לפסול את עצמו מחזקתו, דקרוב הוא אצל עצמו, וקרוב פסול לעדות:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:6:3.english: One does not render himself wicked - He is not deemed credible to disqualify himself from his presumptive status [of fitness], for he is a relative with respect to himself, and a relative is disqualified from testifying.

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:7:1.hebrew: אין נאמנין לפוסלו - ארישא דמתניתין פליג, העדים שאמרו כתב ידינו הוא, אבל אנוסים היינו כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:7:1.english: [They] are not deemed credible to invalidate it - [Rabbi Meir] disagrees with the first clause of our Mishnah: "The witnesses who said, 'It is our handwriting, but we were coerced, etc.'"

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:7:2.hebrew: הפה שהתיר - וכיון דמחמת נפשות קאמרי נאנסנו, לא משוו נפשייהו רשעים. ופסולי עדות דקאמרי, היינו טעמא דלאו בעדותן משוו נפשייהו רשעים, אלא דאמרי קרובים או עבדים היינו, ועכשיו אנו משוחררים:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:7:2.english: The mouth that permitted [it] - And since they say, "We were coerced due to [danger to our] lives," they do not render themselves wicked. And [regarding] "disqualified witnesses" that they say [they were], the reason [they are believed] is that through their testimony they do not render themselves wicked; rather, they say, "We were relatives, or slaves, and now we are freed."

Rashi on Ketubot 18b:7:3.hebrew: בשלמא פסולי עדות - או קטנים: כיון דמודים הם שהשטר כדין נכתב, שההלואה או המקח אמת, אבל "אנחנו לא היינו ראוים, והויא לה כמלוה על פה, או אי מכירה היא — לא נקנה הקרקע בשטר זה", אמר ר"מ דלא מהימני, דא"כ מלוה לא שדי זוזי בכדי, וכי מחתים עדים על שטרו מידק דייק שיהו כשרים:
Rashi on Ketubot 18b:7:3.english: Granted, disqualified witnesses - Or minors: since they admit that the document was written lawfully, that the loan or the purchase is genuine, [and claim,] "However, we were not fit [to testify], and [thus] it is like an oral loan, or if it is a sale, the land was not acquired through this document," Rabbi Meir says that they are not believed, for if [it were] so, a lender does not throw away money for nothing, and when he has witnesses sign on his document, he checks carefully so that they are fit.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:1:1.hebrew: ובכולי בעי דלודי - פירש בקונטרס בב"מ (דף ג: ושם), דאתא לפרש דלא תימא אמאי נשבע, נימא מגו דחשיד אממונא חשיד נמי אשבועתא; ולהכי קאמר "ובכולי בעי דלודי ליה", ולא חשיד אממונא. וקשה לר"י, דהא אמר בפ"ק דב"מ (דף ה:) דלא אמרינן מגו דחשיד אממונא חשיד נמי אשבועתא! ואין לומר דמן התורה חשיד נמי אשבועתא, ומדרבנן הוא דאמרינן דלא חשיד, לפי שראו שהיו מקילין בממון יותר מבשבועה, ותקנו שבועה על החשודים כל זמן שלא נודע שהוא גזלן, שכשר מן התורה עדיין, אבל גזלן ידוע שפסול מן התורה לא תקנו — ולפי זה שבועה שלא שלחתי בו יד היא מדרבנן [ולא הויא דאורייתא אלא שבועה שלא פשעתי בה], והא דכתיב "אם לא שלח", לא שנשבע שלא שלח, אלא ה"ק קרא: נשבע שלא פשע, אימתי? בזמן שלא שלח בו יד, דאם שלח בו יד חייב אפילו שלא פשע, דנתחייב באונסים — דהא גבי נסכא דרבי אבא (שבועות דף לב:) משמע דאי אמר "לא חטפי", היה נשבע להכחיש את העד אע"ג דחשיד אממונא, והתם הויא שבועה דאוריית', דבשבועה דרבנן לא אמרינן "מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם", כדמשמע בפ"ק דב"מ (שם) גבי ההוא רעיא. ונראה דאתא לפרש דלא תקשי: כיון דאין אדם מעיז, יהא נאמן במה שכפר מקצת; וכיון דמחייבינן שבועה, אם כן מחשבו עזות פנים, א"כ יהא נאמן במגו דאי בעי כפר הכל — וקאמר דאין זה עזות מה שכופר קצת. וא"ת: כיון דלא חשיד אשבועתא, למה גזלן פסול לשבועה? ותירץ הר' יהודה חסיד, דדוקא כשהוא חשוד על אותו ממון שבא לישבע, אמרינן דלא חשיד אשבועתא, דעל ידי השבועה יפרוש; אבל אותו ממון שכבר גזל לא יפרוש ע"י השבועה. וגבי ההוא רעיא דחשיב ליה גזלן משום דאכל תרי מינייהו, אע"פ שצריך לפרוע הני תרי דאכל, מ"מ לא יפרוש מן השאר משום שבועה, דמה שמשלם בע"כ אין זה השבה מעליא. וי"מ דגזלן כשר לשבועה מן התורה, דלא חשיד אשבועתא, אלא דמדרבנן פסלוהו כשהוא גזלן. ואם תאמר: ומאי שנא דלעדות פסול, כדכתיב "אל תשת ידך עם רשע וגו'", ולשבועה כשר? וי"ל דבשבועת שקר יש בה עונש גדול, דכתיב בה "לא ינקה", וכדאמר בשבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף לט.) שכל העולם כולו נזדעזע כשאמר הקב"ה "(לא תשבעו ו) לא תשא"; ועוד, דבעדות שקר ליכא אלא "לא תענה", ובשבועת שקר איכא "לא תגזול" ו"לא תשבעו לשקר":
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:1:1.english: And he would have liked to admit to him the entire [loan] - Rashi explained in Bava Metzia (3b and there[abouts]) that [the Gemara] comes to explain [this] so that you should not say: Why does he take an oath? Let us say that since he is suspect regarding money, he is also suspect regarding an oath! And therefore [the Gemara] says, "And he would have liked to admit to him the entire [loan]," and [thus] he is not suspect regarding money. And [this] is difficult for the Ri, for [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (5b) that we do not say "since he is suspect regarding money, he is also suspect regarding an oath"! And one cannot say that by Torah law he is indeed also suspect regarding an oath, and it is by rabbinic decree that we say he is not suspect, because [the Sages] saw that people were more lenient with money than with an oath, and they instituted an oath for those who are suspect so long as it has not become known that he is a robber — who is still fit [to swear] by Torah law — whereas for a known robber, who is disqualified by Torah law, they did not institute [an oath] — and according to this, the oath "that I did not lay a hand upon it" is rabbinic [and it is not a Torah oath; rather, only the oath "that I was not negligent with it" is], and that which is written, "whether he did not lay [his hand]," does not mean that he swears that he did not lay [his hand]; rather, this is what the verse means: he swears that he was not negligent — when? When he did not lay his hand upon it, for if he laid his hand upon it, he is liable even if he was not negligent, since he becomes liable for unavoidable accidents — [this cannot be,] for regarding the silver bar of Rabbi Abba (Shevuot 32b), it is implied that if he had said, "I did not snatch [it]," he would have sworn to contradict the witness even though he was suspect regarding money, and there it is a Torah oath, because for a rabbinic oath we do not say, "since he is unable to swear, he must pay," as is implied in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (ibid.) regarding that shepherd. Rather, it appears [to the Ri] that [the Gemara here] comes to explain [this] so that [the following] difficulty should not arise: Since a person is not brazen [enough to deny a claim completely to his creditor's face], he should be believed regarding what he partially denied; and since we obligate [him to take] an oath, if so, we regard him as brazen-faced; if so, let him be believed through a migo, since if he wanted, he could have denied everything — and [the Gemara] says that what he denies partially is not [considered] brazenness. And if you ask: Since he is not suspect regarding an oath, why is a robber disqualified from taking an oath? Rabbi Yehudah HaChasid answered that specifically when he is suspect regarding that [very] money about which he is coming to swear do we say that he is not suspect regarding an oath, because through the oath he will desist [from keeping it]; however, as for that money which he has already robbed, he will not desist through the oath. And regarding that shepherd, whom [the Gemara] considers a robber because he ate two of [the sheep] — even though he must pay for those two that he ate, nevertheless he will not desist from [keeping] the rest because of an oath, since what he pays against his will is not a proper restitution. And there are those who explain that a robber is fit to take an oath by Torah law, since he is not suspect regarding an oath, and it is only by rabbinic decree that [the Sages] disqualified him when he is a robber. And if you ask: What is the difference, that for testimony he is disqualified — as it is written, "Do not place your hand with a wicked person, etc." — while for an oath he is fit? One can answer that a false oath carries a severe punishment, as it is written regarding it, "[The Lord] will not absolve," and as [the Gemara] states in [the chapter] Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 39a), that the entire world trembled when the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "(You shall not swear and) You shall not take [the name of the Lord your God in vain]." Furthermore, in false testimony there is only [the prohibition of] "You shall not bear [false witness]," whereas in a false oath there is [both] "You shall not rob" and "You shall not swear falsely."

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:3:1.hebrew: הרי אלו נאמנים - וא"ת: ולמה נאמנים? והא מגו במקום עדים הוא, דאנן סהדי שלא היו אנוסים ולא פסולי עדות, דהא לקמן אמרינן "תרי ותרי נינהו"? וי"ל: כיון דהצריכו חכמים קיום, הכא לא חשיב כלל קיום מה שאומרים "כתב ידינו הוא זה", כיון דאינהו גופייהו אמרי תוך כדי דבור "קטנים" או "אנוסים היינו". אבל לקמן חשבינן להו כשני עדים, כיון דכבר מקויים הוא שכתב ידן יוצא ממקום אחר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:3:1.english: They are deemed credible - And if you will say: Why are they deemed credible? Isn't this a migo in the place of witnesses, for we are witnesses [i.e., it is presumed as established testimony] that they were not compelled and not disqualified witnesses, since later on we say they are two against two? And one can answer: Since the Sages required ratification [for a document], here what they say — "this is our handwriting" — is not considered ratification at all, since they themselves say within tokh kedei dibbur [immediately], "We were minors" or "We were compelled." However, later on [in the second clause], we consider them [the signatures in the document] as two witnesses, since it is already ratified because their handwriting emerges from another place.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:3:2.hebrew: אין נאמנים - הכא ליכא לאקשויי דלהימנו במגו דאי בעו אמרי פרוע הוא, דכיון דמקויים הוא הוי מגו במקום עדים, כדפירשנו. ועוד, דחוזרים ומגידים הם, וכיון שהגיד שוב אינו חוזר ומגיד, כדאמרי' בגמרא. ועוד, דבשני עדים לא אמרינן מגו. וברישא נאמנים, משום דאי בעו שתקי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:3:2.english: They are not deemed credible - Here, one cannot raise the difficulty that they should be deemed credible through a migo [reasoning] that if they wanted, they could have said, "[The debt] is paid." For since [the document] is ratified, it is a migo in the face of witnesses, as we explained. And furthermore, they are retracting and testifying again, and once [a witness] has testified, he cannot testify again, as we say in the Gemara. And furthermore, with two witnesses we do not apply a migo. And in the first clause [of the Mishnah], they are deemed credible because if they wanted, they could have remained silent.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:4:1.hebrew: לא שנו אלא שאמרו אנוסים היינו מחמת ממון - דלא מהימני משום דלא משוו נפשייהו רשעים; וקטנים — כדרשב"ל; ופסולי עדות — משום דמלוה גופיה מידק דייק, כדאמרינן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:4:1.english: [The Sages] taught [this] only where they said, "We were compelled due to a monetary [threat]" - for they are not believed because they cannot render themselves wicked; and [when they claim they were] minors — [they are not believed] in accordance with [the statement of] Reish Lakish; and [when they claim they were] disqualified witnesses — [they are not believed] because the lender himself carefully investigates [the witnesses], as we say shortly.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:4:2.hebrew: מחמת נפשות הרי אלו נאמנים - וא"ת: וכי אמרו "קטנים היינו" או "אנוסים מחמת ממון היינו", להימנו במגו דאמרי "אנוסים היינו מחמת נפשות", דהא ברישא דאיכא מגו נאמנים לומר "אנוסים היינו מחמת ממון"? וי"ל, דאונס מחמת נפשות לא שכיח; ועוד, דבשני עדים לא אמרינן מגו, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:4:2.english: Due to [a threat to their] lives, they are deemed credible - And if you ask: When they say, "We were minors," or, "We were compelled due to a monetary [threat]," let them be deemed credible through a migo [claim], since they could have said, "We were compelled due to [a threat to their] lives" — for in the first clause [of the Mishnah], where there is a migo, they are deemed credible to say, "We were compelled due to a monetary [threat]"? And one can answer that compulsion due to [a threat to] lives is uncommon; and furthermore, with two witnesses we do not apply migo, as I have explained.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:6:1.hebrew: ואין אדם משים עצמו רשע - וא"ת והא קסבר רבא דפלגינן דיבורא בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ט: ושם) גבי פלוני רבעני לרצוני ופלוני בא על אשתי, אם כן הכא נהימנו דאנוסים היו, אבל לא מחמת ממון אלא מחמת נפשות, דאליבא דרבא קיימא? וי"ל: כיון דקיום שטרות דרבנן, לא פלגינן דיבורא כדי לפסול השטר. ועוד, דאין לנו לומר מעצמינו דאנוסים היו מחמת נפשות, דאונס מחמת נפשות לא שכיח כדפרישית; אבל התם שכיח שבא על אשת איש אחרת כמו על אשתו, או שרבעו אדם אחר. וכן בהרגתיו בספ"ב דיבמות (דף כה: ושם), יכול להיות דאדם אחר הרגו. אי נמי, שאני הכא, דמחמת ממון או מחמת נפשות הוי פירושא דאנוסים היינו, הלכך לא פלגינן דיבורא; אבל לרצונו ובא על אשתו הוי דיבור בפ"ע. א"נ, הכא עיקר עדות הוא במה שאומרים אנוסים היינו, שבאו לומר שלא ראו המלוה — א"כ מיד עושין עצמן רשעים כיון שחתמו, אם לא יעשו פירוש לדבריהם — הלכך לא שייך הכא פלגינן דיבורא. אבל ההיא דהרגתיו, עיקר עדות הוא לומר שנהרג להשיא את אשתו, וכן פלוני רבעו או בא על אשתו, עיקר עדות להרוג פלוני; הלכך פלגינן דיבורא, ולגבי להשים עצמו רשע או לגבי אשתו לא יהא נאמן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:6:1.english: And one does not render himself wicked - And if you will ask: Does not Rava hold that we split a statement [palginan dibbura] in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (9b and there), regarding [the cases of] "So-and-so sodomized me willingly" and "So-and-so had relations with my wife"? If so, here [too], let us believe them that they were compelled, but not due to a monetary [threat], rather due to [a threat to] lives, for [the halakha] stands in accordance with Rava! And one can answer: Since the ratification of documents is rabbinic, we do not split a statement in order to invalidate the document. And furthermore, we should not say on our own that they were compelled due to [a threat to] lives, since compulsion due to [a threat to] lives is not common, as I have explained; whereas there [in Sanhedrin], it is common that he had relations with another married woman just as with his wife, or that another man sodomized him. And similarly regarding [the case of] "I killed him" at the end of the second chapter of Yevamot (25b and there), it is possible that another person killed him. Alternatively, it is different here, because "due to a monetary [threat]" or "due to [a threat to] lives" is an explanation of "we were compelled," therefore we do not split the statement; whereas "willingly" and "he had relations with my wife" are each an independent statement. Alternatively, here the primary testimony is in what they say, "we were compelled," for they came to say that they did not see the loan — if so, they immediately render themselves wicked since they signed, unless they give an explanation for their words — therefore "we split a statement" does not apply here. Whereas in that [case] of "I killed him," the primary testimony is to say that he was killed in order to permit his wife to remarry; and similarly [in] "So-and-so sodomized him" or "had relations with his wife," the primary testimony is to execute So-and-so; therefore we split the statement, and with respect to rendering himself wicked or with respect to his wife, he is not believed.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:7:1.hebrew: מלוה גופיה מידק דייק - ולרבנן, אפי' מלוה על פה לא הויא, דבעינן שיהא תחלתו וסופו בכשרות, כדאמרי' ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכח. ושם):
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:7:1.english: The lender himself carefully investigates - And according to the Rabbis, it is not even [considered] a verbal loan, for we require that its beginning and its end be in [a state of] fitness, as we say in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 128a, and elsewhere).

Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:7:2.hebrew: קטנים נמי כדרשב"ל - ה"מ למימר "וקטנים נמי משום דמלוה גופיה מידק דייק", אלא דניחא ליה למינקט בכל חד טעמא אחרינא. א"נ, טעמא דריש לקיש גופיה נמי משום דמלוה מידק דייק; והא דלא מייתי דרשב"ל אפסולי עדות, משום דר"ל לא הזכיר אלא קטנים בדבריו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18b:7:2.english: "Minors as well, in accordance with [the statement of] Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish" - [The Gemara] could have said: "And minors as well, because the lender himself ascertains [their fitness]," except that it prefers to give a different reason for each one. Alternatively, the reason of Reish Lakish himself is also because the lender ascertains [their fitness]; and the reason [the Gemara] does not cite [the statement of] Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish regarding disqualified witnesses is because Reish Lakish only mentioned minors in his statement.
